title: Finger push ups tutorial (benefits and risk)
summary: NH presents finger push-ups as an advanced push-up variation: they deload the chest and wrists, shift emphasis to the back (teres major), and strengthen finger tendons and ligaments, useful for rock climbers. Progress from ten fingers down to the thumb; he recalls 20-rep thumb sets at a lighter bodyweight and aims for two-finger reps at 215 lbs.

claims.claim: Finger push-ups are for advanced trainees bored of regular, diamond and other variations; don't try them if you're not good at normal push-ups.
Start finger push-ups with all fingers and ramp up carefully because they are very taxing on the fingers, especially for heavy lifters.
Finger push-ups deload the chest somewhat, put more emphasis on the back (teres major), deload the wrists but strain the fingers.
Finger push-ups strengthen finger ligaments and tendons that most grip work doesn't reach, useful for rock climbers.
Progress finger push-ups from ten fingers to four, three, two, then one (thumb first, as the strongest), then index.
At 170-180 lbs bodyweight NH did sets of 20 thumb-only push-ups and 1-2 reps on the index finger, never any on other single fingers.
His current goal is to do two-finger push-ups at 215 lbs bodyweight.

exercises.name: Finger push-ups
cues: only if good at normal push-ups
exercises.why: finger tendon strength, back emphasis, wrist deload
